body.x: What's Matter Inc., led by CEO Hakyong Kim, will take part in CES 2027, which runs Jan. 6 to Jan. 9 (local time) in Las Vegas, as part of the Gyeonggi Pavilion, to present ModusHome AI Home Core, a spatial intelligence hub built on multiple AI agents, and Quiet-Care, a non-invasive safety care service built on it.

The company will be at Booth 63312 and was named a CES Innovation Awards Honoree in the Smart Home category. Quiet-Care analyzes presence and movement in the home without cameras or wearables. When it detects signs that something is wrong, such as an unusually long stay in one place or no movement, it alerts a guardian. The service is meant to support independent living for older adults and give families peace of mind, and it aims to reduce the burden of complicated device controls or changes in daily habits so that people can keep living in familiar homes, an approach known as aging in place.

ModusHome AI Home Core is an AI edge hub that handles everything from sensor data collection to situation understanding, service recommendations, verification before execution and device control. A local AI agent analyzes data from various sensors and devices to understand the conditions in a space and the user's living patterns. Devices from different brands connect through the Matter standard, and the main data analysis and control stay inside the home, which protects personal information. Cloud AI is used only to interpret natural language, a hybrid structure that cuts the transmission of personal data outside the home and the dependence on the cloud. A technology called Home Intent Memory stores and reuses verified user intent to speed up responses to repeated requests and make better use of AI.

The company will also show four Matter devices developed through a intelligent home service demonstration project run by NIPA: an occupancy sensor, a CO2 sensor with built-in temperature and humidity sensors, a leak sensor and a two-gang smart button with an inertial sensor.

Founded in February 2024, What's Matter specializes in intelligent home solutions based on spatial intelligence. It builds on experience developing and distributing Matter devices and designing and building smart homes. It has carried out senior care demonstration projects with SK Telecom and KT and took part in a 100-household intelligent home service demonstration in 2025. It won NIPA's intelligent home service demonstration and expansion project two times in a row, receiving a total of KRW 1.724 billion in government support. So far it has developed 11 Matter devices and holds 17 Matter certifications, 24 KC certifications and five patents and trademarks. Kim received a Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy commendation in 2024 for contributions to the smart home industry, and the company's on-device AI edge hub won the ETRI President's Award at the 2025 AIoT Innovation Awards.

At CES 2027, What's Matter wants to confirm the value of its products and services in senior care and find partners for overseas joint pilots and commercialization. It plans to propose care packages combined with existing services to companies in care, senior housing, telecommunications, insurance and security, and to work out localization and market entry with partners that have local installation and operating capabilities. Japan, Europe and the United States are the regions it wants to enter first, with an approach built on aging in place, and in the Middle East it is exploring cooperation in senior housing and intelligent homes tied to residential development and healthcare businesses. Home care providers, senior housing operators, telecom, insurance and security companies, and smart home installation and operation specialists are its main targets, and the goal is to move from joint pilots to supply and subscription contracts.

In Korea, the company plans to refine ModusHome AI Home Core and Quiet-Care and check the reliability of anomaly detection, ease of use and the appropriateness of guardian alerts through demonstrations, including participation in Hwaseong City's integrated care project. It is also discussing sleep care and home IoT-based home care businesses with construction companies and security companies that dispatch response teams. With partners found at CES, it plans joint pilots adapted to local housing, living patterns and care operations, backed by an operating system that covers installation and maintenance, guardian alerts, and confirmation and response by care staff. Its main challenges are the cost and staffing needed for overseas certification and privacy regulation review, localization for language and living environments, and securing field operating partners. Senior care also requires winning the trust of users and guardians and agreeing on who responds, and how, when something goes wrong. What's Matter is seeking support for overseas certification and localization costs, verified care partners, local joint pilots and post-show commercialization, and investment and business funding for the move from pilots to initial adoption.

AVING News, a global media company with 21 years of experience covering CES, operates AVING CES Newsroom (avingces.news), a dedicated platform for delivering the latest innovations to global audiences. Publishing more than 1,000 articles and conducting hundreds of on-site video interviews annually, AVING News has helped Korean startups gain international visibility and expand their global reach. At CES 2027, AVING News will operate the AVING TECH TALK broadcast zone at the Venetian Expo (Hall A, Booth 50271), providing on-site coverage and interviews that spotlight Korean companies and their latest innovations.

Ahead of CES 2027, AVING News will host the 3rd Innovation Awards Winners Networking Party at MIK BASE CAMP on Wednesday, November 25, at 5 p.m. The event will also feature individual video interviews with participating companies, with registration available through Eventus. In early December, AVING News will begin its pre-show coverage, including an interview program connecting Korean innovators with U.S. media outlets that regularly cover CES and participate in the Innovation Awards judging process.

After CES 2027 concludes, AVING News will co-host a post-show conference with participating companies to highlight their achievements, strengthen their domestic visibility and enhance their corporate reputation.
